prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, ankle-cut demi statue portrait — a sculpted figure ending at the narrowest point of the lower calf, well above a full foot, the longest of the demi statue family, showing the full leg. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually rounded, deliberately carved tips at the narrowest point of each lower calf, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end there, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Latina woman in telenovela glam makeup — warm golden-bronze skin, a sharp black winged liner, warm terracotta eyeshadow, heavy lashes, strong sculpted contour, large dark eyes with bright real catchlights, a deep berry lip, long voluminous dark-brown waves swept over one shoulder, a fiery, passionate expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a large gold hoop hangs clear of the neck down to the shoulder.

Physique: A giant hourglass frame flaring at both ends — shoulders more than four times a normal woman's width, a colossal chest projecting past them, a big round belly, no waist at all, hips as broad as the shoulders, both thighs, both knees and both calves clearly separate and individually shaped, each calf narrowing smoothly toward its lower end.

Body: From the collarbones down, her whole body — both shoulders, both arms and hands, her chest, belly, hips, both thighs, both knees and both calves — is not painted, covered or clothed but physically carved from ONE solid block of genuine malachite, a rich green stone banded with concentric rings and swirling stripes in varying shades of green, polished to a smooth glossy sheen, completely opaque. It is one continuous sculpted mass, never hollow, with no seam and no skin anywhere, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same stone, the banded rings running unbroken down the length of each leg. At the narrowest point of each lower leg, each one individually curves inward and rounds off into its own smooth, polished tip, a simple rounded column-end, the concentric bands converging at its centre — the two legs stay clearly separate all the way down, never merging, fusing or tapering into a single base — the stone simply reaching its natural end on each leg, both rounded tips resting side by side on the surface beneath her.

Opacity: everything below the collarbones is solid, completely opaque malachite — no light passes through it at any point. It has the same cool, hard, dense solidity throughout, catching light only as bright highlights on its polished surface, never glowing from within. Her face, by contrast, is warm, soft, living flesh, its natural colour nowhere close to the colour of the stone.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones — real skin above, material immediately below. There is no line down the centre of her body. At that line, the stone's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. The rounded tip at the end of each leg is the material's own carved finish, always the clean, deliberate result of a sculpture — never the edge of a photograph. Shards interlock along the collarbone line only.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a deep emerald green on one side and a warm gold on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand (solid material) resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body with the hand (solid material) relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so emerald-green light glances off the left half and gold light glances off the right half, catching in bright reflections. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. Only her face, ears and neck read as real skin. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
